checks: The gauge is subadditive and at most the Euclidean norm divided by r. Applying this to both differences gives its 1/r Lipschitz bound. On the sphere its minimum is at least 1/R, so taking the reciprocal gives R²/r. Adding the term from changing the unit direction gives R+R²/r.

Each ray from the interior point reaches exactly one boundary point. For w,w′ of norm at least r, splitting the difference of w/|w| and w′/|w′| into its numerator difference and normalization difference gives ≤2|w−w′|/r.

Lipschitz graph charts and almost-everywhere differentiability make nonregular boundary points surface-null. If a plane cuts the interior, its intersection with the body boundary is the relative boundary of its full-dimensional section in that plane. A supporting plane meets a strictly convex body at most at one point, whose surface measure is zero because d≥2. Exterior planes give an empty intersection.

The finite union of exceptions stays null under the inverse radial map. The antipodal image is null as an isometric image. Since the sphere has positive surface measure, one direction avoids both sets and yields the two specified endpoints.

Its localized additions assume a specified regular point with singleton support. The present lemma finds a pair of such points from a given interior anchor, simultaneously avoiding the listed planes.
